data.title: Pdcd4-Rictor interaction suppresses mTORC2-PFKFB3 axis and tumorigenesis in NSCLC.
data.authors: Wang Q; Xin Y; Zokaei E et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: NSCLC cell lines; mouse xenograft; human tumour tissue
data.finding: Pdcd4 binds Rictor via residues R105/K108/R110 to disrupt mTORC2 assembly and kinase activity, lowering PFKFB3 levels and suppressing glycolysis and NSCLC tumour growth.
data.abstract_excerpt: Programmed cell death 4 (Pdcd4) is a tumour suppressor and inhibitor of protein translation with emerging translation-independent functions. Pdcd4 suppresses tumorigenesis by disrupting mTORC2 complex formation through binding Rictor. Deletion mapping and site-directed mutagenesis defined the Rictor-binding domain of Pdcd4 and identified residues R105, K108 and R110 as critical. Co-immunoprecipitation and in vitro kinase assays showed that Pdcd4 binding to Rictor disrupted mTORC2 assembly and inhibited its kinase activity.

extracted_findings.effect: Disrupted mTORC2 assembly and kinase activity, degraded PFKFB3, suppressed glycolysis and tumour growth
